blocks.x: All ashore for some autumn adventures! As the leaves begin to turn and the air gets that unmistakable crispness, fall is the perfect time to escape the city for a day of foliage, fresh air, and a little seasonal fun. But, of course, one of the trickiest parts of planning a day trip is figuring out how to actually get there.
But what if getting there could be part of the experience, too? One NYC happening is ensuring that that’s the case.

Circle Line’s beloved Bear Mountain Oktoberfest Cruise is back for 2026, sailing alongside its Hudson River Fall Foliage Cruise for the ultimate autumn escape. Guests can skip the traffic and crowded trains and trade the city streets for the Hudson River, where you’ll sail north from Midtown as the skyline gives way to the colorful cliffs and foliage of the Hudson Valley.

Source / Circle Line Cruises
Choose Your Adventure: 8-Hour Excursion vs. 4-Hour Scenic Sail
Circle Line offers two distinct ways to experience Oktoberfest on the Hudson, depending on how much time you have to spare:

Hudson River Fall Foliage Cruise (4 Hours): A condensed, non-stop round-trip option sailing up to Hook Mountain. It delivers the exact same onboard Oktoberfest energy, live music, and festive menu without docking ashore—perfect for a half-day getaway.

Bear Mountain Oktoberfest Cruise (8 Hours): The full-day marquee excursion. Includes a 50-mile journey north to Bear Mountain State Park with roughly three hours ashore to hike, explore, or relax before the return trip.

Source / Circle Line Cruises
What you’ll see along the way

One of the biggest draws of the cruise is that you don’t have to wait until you reach Bear Mountain to start sightseeing. As you travel up the Hudson River, you’ll be treated to front-row, panoramic views of some of the region’s most striking natural landmarks and engineering marvels:
Engineering Icons: Cruise directly beneath the towering George Washington Bridge and the Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge.
Dramatic Geology: Take in the sheer face of the Palisades Cliffs and the 800-foot heights of Hook Mountain draped in fall color.

Historic Sites & Wildlife: Catch sight of the medieval-style architecture of The Cloisters nestled in Fort Tryon Park, and keep an eye out for native raptors, including hawks, ospreys, and bald eagles soaring above the river.

Source / Circle Line Cruises
The Bear Mountain Experience: Exploring Ashore
For those on the 8-hour excursion, docking at Bear Mountain State Park unlocks three hours of outdoor exploration:

Hiking Trails: Access miles of forested trails catering to all fitness levels, ranging from casual walking paths around the park to steeper climbs up the mountain for panoramic views of the Hudson Valley.
Hessian Lake: Take a leisurely stroll along the paved path looping around the water, or rent a pedal boat to venture out onto the lake.
Trailside Museums & Zoo: Visit the local zoo and environmental centers home to native wildlife, including black bears, eagles, and reptiles.

Source / Circle Line Cruises
What To Know Before You Go
Plan ahead to ensure a seamless trip on the water:
Sailing Dates: Weekends starting September 19th through November 8th, 2026.
Departure Location: All cruises depart from Pier 83 at West 42nd Street and 12th Avenue in Midtown Manhattan.
Timing: Boarding begins at 8:30 AM, and the vessel departs promptly at 9:00 AM sharp.
